newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE STAGES GREAT IRISH OPEN FINISH.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE STAGES GREAT IRISH OPEN FINISH.

text.p: Britain's Colin Montgomerie staged a remarkable repeat Irish Open victory on Sunday.
A Druid's Glen course record 62 wiped out his three shots deficit on long-time leader Lee Westwood and boosted him to a seven-shot winning margin.

Montgomerie's irresistible nine-under-par round, two better than the previous best, and late mistakes by fellow Briton Westwood, leader since the first round, caused a 10-shot swing in the final round.
After catching his playing-partner Westwood by the third, Montgomerie moved ahead by the eighth and then left his young English rival in his wake.
He totalled a 15 under-par 269, including one eagle and eight birdies in his closing round. The form even surprised the Scot himself.
"My good rounds in majors, especially that 65 a few weeks ago at the Congressional in the US Open, are pretty special. But this has to rank very, very highly," he said.
"With the field we had...it was almost like a major, so to play golf at that level has to make it pretty special.
It was Montgomerie's second European Tour victory in four weeks, bringing him right into contention for a record fifth successive European order of merit title after a slow start to the year.
His previous victory also came when he fended off a determined bid by Westwood in the European Grand Prix last month.
Westwood finished second on 276 with compatriot and six-times major winner Nick Faldo third, two shots behind.
European rankings leader Ian Woosnam of Wales shared fourth place with Sweden's Michael Jonzon on 280. Spain's Jose Maria Olazabal finished a stroke further back in sixth.
Montgomerie refused to be drawn into forecasting his chances in the British Open in 10 days.
But he said: "This win is another confidence-booster and obviously my expectations get higher every time I win."
